finding: Wazuh 4.12.0 all-in-one (manager, indexer, dashboard, Filebeat) installed on the Ubuntu 20.04 VM; installer reported "Installation finished" at 22:48:01 UTC on 18 Oct.
limitation: Run 5 was the fifth attempt; the administrator password line is redacted.

finding: The installer option -i printed "Hardware checks ignored"; in this version -i skips the hardware check and is not an interactive mode as the manual states.
limitation: Read from log lines of runs 2 and 5.

finding: After run 5 the manager, dashboard and Filebeat were active and the indexer had failed; ports 1514, 1515, 55000 and 443 were listening.
limitation: Status shown at one moment only.

finding: The indexer failed on boot with "start operation timed out" at 23:01:57 UTC; a manual start succeeded and 9200 listened on 127.0.0.1.
limitation: Root cause (slow start under load) is inferred, not measured.

finding: A systemd drop-in with TimeoutStartSec=900 was created to prevent a repeat.
limitation: Not tested by a second reboot.

finding: Run 1 failed at 14:41:23 UTC (15 Oct) because the dashboard web application did not initialise; the VM had 4.3 GiB RAM and 2 vCPU; no out-of-memory kill was found.
limitation: Resource shortage is the likely cause, not proven; later runs also changed other things.

finding: Run 2 failed with "Cannot import Wazuh GPG key" because ens33 had no IPv4 address at that moment.
The netplan file named the interface enp0s3 while the real interface is ens33; it was corrected with sed and netplan apply.
limitation: That the wrong name caused every lost lease is inferred.

finding: Runs 3 and 4 failed on package downloads (connection refused, IPv6 unreachable) from packages.wazuh.com; run 4 spent 72 minutes on the indexer before failing at Filebeat (21:59:55 UTC).
limitation: The cause is the internet path; the remote server was not examined.

finding: Packages were pre-downloaded with apt-get --download-only (185 MB in 9 min 40 s at 318 kB/s) and copied to ~/wazuh-debs; run 5 then completed in 15 minutes.
limitation: The installer also used the local apt cache; which files it took is not shown.

finding: Windows could not reach the VM (ssh, Test-NetConnection time out) because the host adapter VMware Network Adapter VMnet8 was "Not Present"; Windows was only on Wi-Fi.
limitation: Why the adapter disappeared is not known.

finding: After Virtual Network Editor > Restore Defaults, VMnet8 was Up at 192.168.119.1 and the VM leased 192.168.119.128 (earlier 192.168.152.131).
limitation: The new NAT subnet came from the restore, not from a planned design.

finding: The dashboard login page loaded at https://192.168.119.128/app/login with a "Not secure" warning (self-signed certificate); ports 443 and 22 tested True from Windows.
limitation: Certificate chain not examined.

finding: Agent 001 "Windows-SOC-Lab" was created with manage_agents (IP any); a repeated Add attempt was refused as a duplicate name.
The agent connected to 192.168.119.128:1514/tcp at 08:34:16 local (15:34:16 UTC); dashboard and agent_control show it Active (Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, v4.12.0).
The only change made to ossec.conf was one <directories realtime="yes" check_all="yes" report_changes="yes"> line for SensitiveFiles (Compare-Object).
limitation: check_all and report_changes go beyond the manual (realtime only).

finding: After restart, ossec.log at 08:45:43 local shows the SensitiveFiles path monitored with hash_md5, hash_sha1, hash_sha256, report_changes and realtime.
Run 1: three alerts for secret_plan.txt at 08:50:33.922 (added, level 5), 08:51:19.230 (modified, level 7) and 08:52:04.227 (deleted, level 7) local.
limitation: No local record of hashes for run 1 (log folder missing).
Script times have 1 s resolution.

finding: Rule IDs and levels are 554 (5), 550 (7) and 553 (7); the manager alerts.log lists the same two sequences.

Alert values match the local record: after create size 31 and SHA-256 482BC551...6C1A5D; after modify size 82 and SHA-256 EADB58EB...13085C; sha256_before of the modified alert equals the create hash.
limitation: Only SHA-256 and size were compared with the local record; MD5 and SHA-1 come from the alert only.

finding: The modified alert reports changed attributes size, mtime, md5, sha1, sha256, and syscheck.diff shows the added line.
The alert maps to MITRE T1565.001 (Stored Data Manipulation, tactic Impact) and to PCI DSS 11.5, GDPR II_5.1.f, HIPAA 164.312.c.1/c.2, NIST 800-53 SI.7 and TSC controls.
limitation: Mappings come from the ruleset; they are not a compliance assessment.

finding: The alert shows the file owner (uname_after Administrators, uid_after S-1-5-32-544) but not the process or user that made the change.
limitation: Real-time mode without whodata; whodata was not tested.

finding: Wazuh and the VM use UTC; the Windows host clock is UTC-7 (script prints local 08:58:10 and UTC 15:58:10); the dashboard shows the browser/host time.
The overview showed 484 medium and 391 low severity alerts in 24 hours for one endpoint; only 6 were syscheck events from the test.
limitation: The other alerts were not broken down by rule group.

finding: The VM banner reports Ubuntu 20.04 LTS past the end of standard support (31 May 2025) and "Failed to connect to changelogs.ubuntu.com".
A frequency-based custom rule and canary files are proposed for ransomware detection (answer 3).
limitation: Proposed only; not deployed or tested in this lab.
